questions.prompt: Which phrase is most polite when asking a classmate to repeat a point?
questions.correctAnswer: Please say that again.
questions.explanation: Please makes the request respectful and suitable for classroom discussion.
questions.learningOutcome: Use polite expressions when seeking clarification in a conversation.

questions.prompt: In the instruction read the question, underline key words, then write your answer, what should be done second?
questions.correctAnswer: underline key words
questions.explanation: The second action named in the instruction is to underline key words.
questions.learningOutcome: Follow ordered oral instructions by identifying the correct step.

questions.prompt: Which word means nearly the same as repair?
questions.correctAnswer: mend
questions.explanation: To mend something is to repair it.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify synonyms for common grade-level words.

questions.prompt: Which word is the opposite of generous?
questions.correctAnswer: selfish
questions.explanation: Generous means willing to give, while selfish means thinking only of oneself.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify antonyms in familiar contexts.

questions.prompt: Which word is an abstract noun in the sentence Kindness helps a team work well?
questions.correctAnswer: Kindness
questions.explanation: Kindness names a quality that cannot be touched or seen directly.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise abstract nouns in simple sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a proper noun correctly?
options: We visited Nakuru during the holiday.
We visited town during the holiday.
We visited place during the holiday.
We visited county during the holiday.
questions.correctAnswer: We visited Nakuru during the holiday.
questions.explanation: Nakuru is the name of a specific place, so it is a proper noun.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify proper nouns and capitalise them correctly.

questions.prompt: What is the plural form of child?
questions.correctAnswer: children
questions.explanation: Children is the irregular plural form of child.
questions.learningOutcome: Use common irregular plural nouns correctly.

questions.prompt: Which word is an adverb in the sentence Wanjala spoke confidently during the debate?
questions.correctAnswer: confidently
questions.explanation: Confidently tells how Wanjala spoke, so it is an adverb.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify adverbs that describe how actions are done.

questions.prompt: Which punctuation mark should end the sentence Where is the science corner?
questions.correctAnswer: question mark
questions.explanation: A direct question should end with a question mark.
questions.learningOutcome: Use question marks to punctuate direct questions.

questions.prompt: Which word is an interjection in the sentence Wow, the poem was exciting?
questions.correctAnswer: Wow
questions.explanation: Wow expresses a sudden feeling, so it is an interjection.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify interjections used to express feelings.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is in the present perfect tense?
questions.correctAnswer: She has finished her homework.
questions.explanation: Has finished shows an action completed before now with present importance.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise the present perfect tense in familiar sentences.

questions.prompt: Which word has the prefix re- meaning again?
questions.correctAnswer: rewrite
questions.explanation: Rewrite means to write again, so re- adds the idea of again.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise common prefixes and their meanings.

questions.prompt: Which expression is suitable for disagreeing politely during group work?
options: I see your point, but I think we should try another way.
questions.correctAnswer: I see your point, but I think we should try another way.
questions.explanation: A polite disagreement respects the other speaker before giving a different view.
questions.learningOutcome: Express disagreement respectfully in classroom discussions.

questions.prompt: Which title best fits a paragraph about saving rainwater and closing taps after use?
questions.correctAnswer: Conserving Water
questions.explanation: The details are about using water carefully, so the title matches the main idea.
questions.learningOutcome: Select a suitable title for a short text based on its main idea.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: The group of learners ___ ready for the presentation.
questions.correctAnswer: is
questions.explanation: Group is a singular collective noun here, so it takes the verb is.
questions.learningOutcome: Use verbs that agree with collective nouns in context.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the past continuous tense correctly?
options: The pupils were reading when the bell rang.
The pupils read when the bell rings.
The pupils will be read when the bell rang.
The pupils are read when the bell rang.
questions.correctAnswer: The pupils were reading when the bell rang.
questions.explanation: Were reading shows an action that was continuing in the past.
questions.learningOutcome: Use the past continuous tense to describe ongoing past actions.

questions.prompt: Which word best joins the sentence We stayed indoors ___ the rain stopped?
questions.correctAnswer: until
questions.explanation: Until shows the time when the action of staying indoors ended.
questions.learningOutcome: Use conjunctions to show time relationships in sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly to show ownership by one teacher?
options: The teacher's guide is on the desk.
The teachers guide is on the desk.
The teachers' guide is on the desk.
The teacher guide's is on the desk.
questions.correctAnswer: The teacher's guide is on the desk.
questions.explanation: Teacher's shows that one teacher owns the guide.
questions.learningOutcome: Use apostrophes to show singular possession.

questions.prompt: Which word completes the sentence The class chose ___ captain after the discussion?
questions.correctAnswer: its
questions.explanation: Its shows possession by the class and does not need an apostrophe.
questions.learningOutcome: Use possessive pronouns correctly in sentences.

questions.prompt: Read: The sky darkened and the wind became cold. What is likely to happen next?
options: The moon will rise at noon.
questions.correctAnswer: It may rain soon.
questions.explanation: Dark clouds and cold wind are clues that rain may be coming.
questions.learningOutcome: Make reasonable predictions from clues in a short text.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses commas correctly in a list?
options: We carried maize, beans, rice, and flour.
We carried, maize beans rice and flour.
We carried maize beans, rice and, flour.
We carried maize, beans rice, and flour.
questions.correctAnswer: We carried maize, beans, rice, and flour.
questions.explanation: Commas can separate items in a list so the meaning is clear.
questions.learningOutcome: Use commas to separate items in a list.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a modal verb to show advice?
options: You should revise before the test.
You are revising before the test.
questions.correctAnswer: You should revise before the test.
questions.explanation: Should is a modal verb commonly used to give advice.
questions.learningOutcome: Use modal verbs to express advice and obligation.

questions.prompt: Which word is formed by adding the suffix -ful correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: hopeful
questions.explanation: Hopeful is formed by adding -ful to hope to mean full of hope.
questions.learningOutcome: Form words correctly using common suffixes.

questions.prompt: Which word best completes the sentence The learners shared the books ___ themselves?
questions.correctAnswer: among
questions.explanation: Among is used when more than two people or things are involved.
questions.learningOutcome: Use prepositions accurately in familiar contexts.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is written in direct speech?
options: Asha said, I need a pencil.
Asha said that she needed a pencil.
Asha was looking for a pencil.
questions.correctAnswer: Asha said, I need a pencil.
questions.explanation: Direct speech gives the speaker's exact words after the reporting clause.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise direct speech in simple sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best reports Asha said, I am ready?
options: Asha said that she was ready.
Asha says that I am ready.
Asha said that she is ready tomorrow.
Asha ready said that was she.
questions.correctAnswer: Asha said that she was ready.
questions.explanation: Reported speech changes I to she and am to was when reporting in the past.
questions.learningOutcome: Change simple direct speech into reported speech.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a relative pronoun correctly?
options: The pupil who won the race is my friend.
The pupil where won the race is my friend.
The pupil when won the race is my friend.
The pupil what won the race is my friend.
questions.correctAnswer: The pupil who won the race is my friend.
questions.explanation: Who refers to a person and connects the extra information to pupil.
questions.learningOutcome: Use relative pronouns to join related ideas.

questions.prompt: Which option is a complete sentence?
questions.correctAnswer: The librarian opened the door.
questions.explanation: A complete sentence has a subject and a complete idea.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify complete sentences and sentence fragments.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the comparative form correctly?
options: This route is safer than the old route.
This route is safest than the old route.
This route is more safer than the old route.
This route safe than the old route.
questions.correctAnswer: This route is safer than the old route.
questions.explanation: Safer compares two routes and is the standard comparative form.
questions.learningOutcome: Use comparative adjectives to compare two things.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a superlative adjective correctly?
options: The cleanest desk won a badge.
The cleaner desk of all won a badge.
The most cleanest desk won a badge.
The clean desk than all won a badge.
questions.correctAnswer: The cleanest desk won a badge.
questions.explanation: Cleanest compares one desk with all the others.
questions.learningOutcome: Use superlative adjectives correctly in sentences.

questions.prompt: Read: Otieno watered the seedlings every evening, so they grew strong. What caused the seedlings to grow strong?
options: The seedlings were in a story.
questions.correctAnswer: Otieno watered them every evening.
questions.explanation: The text shows that regular watering caused the seedlings to grow strong.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify cause and effect relationships in short texts.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a fact rather than an opinion?
options: The school library has three shelves of storybooks.
Storybooks are the most exciting books.
The library is more beautiful than all rooms.
questions.correctAnswer: The school library has three shelves of storybooks.
questions.explanation: A fact can be checked, while the other options express personal views or exaggerations.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish facts from opinions in simple texts.

questions.prompt: Which opening is best for a friendly letter to a cousin?
questions.correctAnswer: Dear Brian,
questions.explanation: A friendly letter begins with a greeting to the person receiving it.
questions.learningOutcome: Use the correct greeting in informal letter writing.

questions.prompt: Which detail best supports the topic sentence Our class cares for the environment?
options: We plant trees around the school compound.
Our timetable has English on Tuesday.
questions.correctAnswer: We plant trees around the school compound.
questions.explanation: Planting trees is an action that shows care for the environment.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose supporting details that match a topic sentence.

questions.prompt: Which word has the same vowel sound as seat?
questions.correctAnswer: meet
questions.explanation: Seat and meet share the long ee vowel sound.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify similar vowel sounds in spoken words.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the homophone their correctly?
options: The pupils packed they are books.
questions.correctAnswer: The pupils packed their books.
questions.explanation: Their shows that the books belong to the pupils.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose the correct homophone for a sentence context.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the article an correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: She carried an umbrella.
questions.explanation: An is used before a word that begins with a vowel sound.
questions.learningOutcome: Use a and an correctly before nouns.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is most suitable for ending an oral report?
questions.correctAnswer: Thank you for listening.
questions.explanation: A courteous closing thanks the audience after a presentation.
questions.learningOutcome: Use appropriate openings and closings in oral presentations.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the future continuous tense correctly?
options: We shall be cleaning the compound at ten o'clock.
We cleaned the compound at ten o'clock.
We clean the compound at ten o'clock.
We are clean the compound at ten o'clock.
questions.correctAnswer: We shall be cleaning the compound at ten o'clock.
questions.explanation: Shall be cleaning shows an action that will be continuing at a future time.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise the future continuous tense in sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best combines these ideas: The bell rang. The learners entered class.
options: When the bell rang, the learners entered class.
The bell the learners rang entered class.
Class rang the bell entered learners.
questions.correctAnswer: When the bell rang, the learners entered class.
questions.explanation: The sentence joins the two ideas clearly and shows the time relationship.
questions.learningOutcome: Combine related ideas into clear compound or complex sentences.

questions.prompt: Read: Njeri checked the spelling, added a missing full stop, and improved one weak sentence. Which writing stage was she doing?
questions.correctAnswer: editing
questions.explanation: Editing involves checking language, punctuation, spelling, and sentence quality.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify stages of the writing process from learner actions.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best changes The headteacher opened the library into passive voice?
options: The library was opened by the headteacher.
The headteacher was opened by the library.
questions.correctAnswer: The library was opened by the headteacher.
questions.explanation: In passive voice, the library receives the action of being opened.
questions.learningOutcome: Change simple active sentences into passive voice.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best changes The match was won by our team into active voice?
options: Our team was won by the match.
questions.correctAnswer: Our team won the match.
questions.explanation: In active voice, the doer of the action comes before the verb.
questions.learningOutcome: Change simple passive sentences into active voice.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a conditional idea correctly?
options: If we leave early, we shall arrive on time.
If we leave early, we arrived yesterday.
We shall if early arrive leave.
questions.correctAnswer: If we leave early, we shall arrive on time.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses if to show a condition and a likely result.
questions.learningOutcome: Use conditional sentences to show possible results.

questions.prompt: Read: The hall was packed, yet everyone listened quietly. What does yet show in the sentence?
questions.correctAnswer: contrast
questions.explanation: Yet joins two ideas that are different from what a reader might expect.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how conjunctions link ideas in sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses dialogue punctuation most clearly?
options: Musa asked, Are we visiting the museum today?
Musa asked Are we visiting the museum today
Musa asked, are we visiting the museum today.
Musa asked are, we visiting the museum today?
questions.correctAnswer: Musa asked, Are we visiting the museum today?
questions.explanation: The comma introduces the spoken words and the question ends with a question mark.
questions.learningOutcome: Punctuate simple dialogue in narrative writing.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has the clearest subject and predicate?
options: The school choir practised after lunch.
questions.correctAnswer: The school choir practised after lunch.
questions.explanation: The school choir is the subject and practised after lunch tells what it did.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify complete sentence structure with subject and predicate.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best uses a precise verb?
options: The athlete sprinted to the finish line.
The athlete went to the finish line.
The athlete did to the finish line.
The athlete made to the finish line.
questions.correctAnswer: The athlete sprinted to the finish line.
questions.explanation: Sprinted tells exactly how the athlete moved.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose precise verbs to make writing clearer.

questions.prompt: Which sentence appeals most clearly to the sense of hearing?
options: The drum echoed across the field.
questions.correctAnswer: The drum echoed across the field.
questions.explanation: Echoed describes sound, so the sentence appeals to hearing.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sensory details in descriptive texts.

questions.prompt: Read: The small shop sold bread, milk, soap, and exercise books. Which word is a general name for these items?
questions.correctAnswer: goods
questions.explanation: Goods are items that can be sold in a shop.
questions.learningOutcome: Use context to choose the meaning of unfamiliar words.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best summarises a story in which a learner lost a book, searched for it, and found it in the library?
options: A learner looked for a missing book and found it in the library.
A learner ate lunch near the gate.
A book was blue and had many pages.
The library had windows and chairs.
questions.correctAnswer: A learner looked for a missing book and found it in the library.
questions.explanation: A summary gives the main events without unnecessary details.
questions.learningOutcome: Summarise the main events of a short story.

questions.prompt: Which topic sentence best fits details about washing hands, covering food, and cleaning utensils?
options: Sports are played in many schools.
The sun rises in the east.
questions.correctAnswer: Good hygiene helps prevent illness.
questions.explanation: All the details are ways of keeping clean and healthy.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose topic sentences that match supporting details.

questions.prompt: Which sentence does not belong in a paragraph about preparing for a debate?
options: The tomatoes were ripe in the garden.
We arranged our points in order.
questions.correctAnswer: The tomatoes were ripe in the garden.
questions.explanation: The sentence about tomatoes is not connected to debate preparation.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify irrelevant sentences in a paragraph.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the word light as an adjective?
options: The light bag was easy to carry.
questions.correctAnswer: The light bag was easy to carry.
questions.explanation: Light describes the bag, so it is used as an adjective.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise how one word can be used as different parts of speech.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a phrasal verb correctly?
options: Please look after the seedlings during break time.
Please look the seedlings after during break time.
Please after look the seedlings during break time.
Please seedlings look after during break time.
questions.correctAnswer: Please look after the seedlings during break time.
questions.explanation: Look after means take care of, and the words are arranged correctly.
questions.learningOutcome: Use common phrasal verbs correctly in context.

questions.prompt: Which option is the best reason for taking notes while listening to a talk?
options: Notes help the listener remember important points.
Notes make the speaker talk faster.
Notes replace the need to listen.
Notes are only for drawing pictures.
questions.correctAnswer: Notes help the listener remember important points.
questions.explanation: Good notes record key ideas so they can be reviewed later.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of note-taking during oral presentations.

questions.prompt: Which question would best help a speaker explain more about conserving water?
options: Can you give an example of saving water at home?
How many shoes do you own?
questions.correctAnswer: Can you give an example of saving water at home?
questions.explanation: The question asks for more information about the topic being discussed.
questions.learningOutcome: Ask relevant questions to extend an oral discussion.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best uses formal language for a school notice?
options: All learners should report to the hall at 2 p.m.
Everyone, come quickly if you feel like it.
Hey people, go to the hall.
You all better show up somewhere.
questions.correctAnswer: All learners should report to the hall at 2 p.m.
questions.explanation: Formal notices use clear, respectful, and precise language.
questions.learningOutcome: Use formal language in notices and school messages.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best completes the notice: Lost: A blue lunch box. Found by anyone should ___
options: return it to the class teacher.
questions.correctAnswer: return it to the class teacher.
questions.explanation: A lost-and-found notice should tell the finder what helpful action to take.
questions.learningOutcome: Write clear instructions in short functional texts.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best uses a transition word to show contrast?
options: The path was muddy; however, we reached school on time.
The path was muddy; therefore, the path was muddy.
The path was muddy; first, it was a path.
The path was muddy; beside, we reached school.
questions.correctAnswer: The path was muddy; however, we reached school on time.
questions.explanation: However introduces an idea that contrasts with the muddy path.
questions.learningOutcome: Use transition words to connect ideas in writing.

questions.prompt: Read: The crowd cheered as the young poet stepped forward smiling. What mood is suggested?
questions.correctAnswer: happy
questions.explanation: Cheering and smiling suggest a happy mood.
questions.learningOutcome: Infer mood from details in a short text.

questions.prompt: Which line from a poem uses alliteration?
options: Busy bees buzzed beside the beans.
The river flowed through the valley.
questions.correctAnswer: Busy bees buzzed beside the beans.
questions.explanation: Alliteration repeats the initial b sound in several nearby words.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify simple sound patterns in poems.

questions.prompt: Which word best describes a character who returns extra change to a shopkeeper?
questions.correctAnswer: honest
questions.explanation: Returning extra change shows truthfulness and fairness.
questions.learningOutcome: Infer character traits from actions in a story.

questions.prompt: Which word best completes the analogy: Teacher is to classroom as doctor is to ___?
questions.correctAnswer: hospital
questions.explanation: A teacher commonly works in a classroom, and a doctor commonly works in a hospital.
questions.learningOutcome: Use word relationships to complete simple analogies.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the word beside correctly?
options: The water bottle is beside the desk.
The water bottle is beside carefully.
The water bottle is beside yesterday.
The water bottle is beside because.
questions.correctAnswer: The water bottle is beside the desk.
questions.explanation: Beside shows position next to something.
questions.learningOutcome: Use prepositions of place accurately in sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best corrects this run-on sentence: We planted trees they grew well?
options: We planted trees, and they grew well.
We planted trees they grew well again.
Trees we planted grew they well.
We planted and trees grew they.
questions.correctAnswer: We planted trees, and they grew well.
questions.explanation: The revision separates and joins two complete ideas clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise run-on sentences into clear sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a colon correctly before a list?
options: Bring these items: a pen, a ruler, and a notebook.
Bring these items a pen: a ruler, and a notebook.
Bring: these items a pen, a ruler, and a notebook.
Bring these: items: a pen, a ruler, and a notebook.
questions.correctAnswer: Bring these items: a pen, a ruler, and a notebook.
questions.explanation: A colon can introduce a list after a complete introductory phrase.
questions.learningOutcome: Use colons to introduce simple lists.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best uses an adverb of frequency?
options: We usually sweep the classroom before assembly.
questions.correctAnswer: We usually sweep the classroom before assembly.
questions.explanation: Usually tells how often the action happens.
questions.learningOutcome: Use adverbs of frequency in everyday sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows the best way to introduce yourself in an interview practice?
options: Good morning, my name is Leila and I am pleased to meet you.
Why do you need my name?
I do not want to speak.
questions.correctAnswer: Good morning, my name is Leila and I am pleased to meet you.
questions.explanation: A good introduction is polite, clear, and suitable for the situation.
questions.learningOutcome: Use appropriate language when introducing oneself in formal situations.

questions.prompt: Which revision best improves the sentence The girl walked slowly to the front?
options: The girl tiptoed to the front, careful not to disturb the class.
The girl walked slowly slowly to the front.
The girl went front slow class.
The girl did walking to front.
questions.correctAnswer: The girl tiptoed to the front, careful not to disturb the class.
questions.explanation: The revision uses a precise verb and adds a useful reason for the action.
questions.learningOutcome: Improve sentences by using precise verbs and meaningful details.

questions.prompt: Read: Although the road was dusty, the runners kept a steady pace. What does although show?
questions.correctAnswer: contrast between difficulty and action
questions.explanation: Although introduces a difficulty that did not stop the runners.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how subordinating conjunctions show relationships between ideas.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best changes The learners said, We have completed the project into reported speech?
options: The learners said that they had completed the project.
The learners said that we have completed the project.
The learners say that they completed the project tomorrow.
The learners said completed had they the project.
questions.correctAnswer: The learners said that they had completed the project.
questions.explanation: Reported speech changes we to they and have completed to had completed after said.
questions.learningOutcome: Report statements using suitable pronoun and tense changes.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best supports the opinion Reading every day improves language skills?
options: Daily reading introduces learners to new words and sentence patterns.
Books can have covers of different colours.
Some shelves are made of wood.
A library may have a door and windows.
questions.correctAnswer: Daily reading introduces learners to new words and sentence patterns.
questions.explanation: A strong reason explains how daily reading helps language skills.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose reasons that support an opinion clearly.

questions.prompt: Which paragraph is most coherent?
options: We prepared the seedbed. We planted sukuma wiki seedlings. We watered them every morning.
We prepared the seedbed. My shoe is black. The moon was bright.
Seedlings need water. I lost a ruler. The bus arrived late.
The bell rang. Bananas ripened. A chair stood near the wall.
questions.correctAnswer: We prepared the seedbed. We planted sukuma wiki seedlings. We watered them every morning.
questions.explanation: The sentences stay on one topic and follow a logical order.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate whether sentences in a paragraph are connected and ordered.

questions.prompt: Read: Amina shared her umbrella with a younger learner during the rain. Which theme best fits this action?
questions.correctAnswer: Kindness helps others.
questions.explanation: Sharing an umbrella shows kindness and care for another person.
questions.learningOutcome: Infer a simple theme from a character's action.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best uses imagery to describe a market?
options: Bright tomatoes filled the stalls as vendors called to passing shoppers.
The market was a place with things.
People were there and items existed.
A market is somewhere for buying.
questions.correctAnswer: Bright tomatoes filled the stalls as vendors called to passing shoppers.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses clear sights and sounds to help the reader imagine the market.
questions.learningOutcome: Use sensory details to create vivid descriptions.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best corrects the unclear pronoun reference in When Moraa met Fatuma, she was carrying a violin?
options: When Moraa met Fatuma, Moraa was carrying a violin.
When Moraa met Fatuma, she and her had it.
When Moraa met Fatuma, carrying was she.
When she met her, the violin was carrying.
questions.correctAnswer: When Moraa met Fatuma, Moraa was carrying a violin.
questions.explanation: Repeating Moraa makes it clear who was carrying the violin.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise unclear pronoun references for clear meaning.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses parallel structure correctly?
options: The club teaches reading, writing, and speaking.
The club teaches reading, to write, and speech.
The club teaches to read, writing, and spoken.
The club teaches read, wrote, and speaking.
questions.correctAnswer: The club teaches reading, writing, and speaking.
questions.explanation: Reading, writing, and speaking follow the same grammatical pattern.
questions.learningOutcome: Use parallel structure in lists and connected ideas.

questions.prompt: Which question would produce the most detailed interview answer from a school gardener?
options: How do you decide which vegetables to plant each season?
questions.correctAnswer: How do you decide which vegetables to plant each season?
questions.explanation: The question is open-ended and invites explanation.
questions.learningOutcome: Ask open-ended questions that invite detailed responses.

questions.prompt: Read: The speaker folded his arms, avoided eye contact, and mumbled. What should he improve most?
questions.correctAnswer: body language and voice projection
questions.explanation: Eye contact, posture, and clear speech affect how well an audience receives a message.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate non-verbal and vocal features in oral presentations.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best changes this note into a clear instruction: litter bin after snack?
options: Put litter in the bin after eating your snack.
questions.correctAnswer: Put litter in the bin after eating your snack.
questions.explanation: The revised instruction states the action, object, place, and time clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Write clear instructions using complete sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best uses reported question form for Did you finish the work?
options: The teacher asked whether I had finished the work.
The teacher asked did I finished the work.
The teacher asked whether did I finish the work.
The teacher asked I finish did the work.
questions.correctAnswer: The teacher asked whether I had finished the work.
questions.explanation: A reported yes-or-no question can use whether and changes the word order.
questions.learningOutcome: Report simple yes-or-no questions accurately.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses both and correctly to join equal ideas?
options: Both the speaker and the audience were prepared.
Both the speaker or the audience were prepared.
Both the speaker but the audience were prepared.
Both the speaker because the audience were prepared.
questions.correctAnswer: Both the speaker and the audience were prepared.
questions.explanation: Both pairs naturally with and to connect two equal nouns.
questions.learningOutcome: Use correlative conjunctions to connect balanced ideas.

questions.prompt: Which option best explains the idiom lend a hand?
questions.correctAnswer: help someone
questions.explanation: To lend a hand means to help with a task.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret common idioms from context.

questions.prompt: Read: We cannot carry the heavy box alone. Let us lend a hand. What does lend a hand mean here?
questions.correctAnswer: help carry the box
questions.explanation: The context shows that help is needed with the heavy box.
questions.learningOutcome: Use context to interpret figurative expressions.

questions.prompt: Which plan best fits a story about resolving a disagreement during group work?
options: Beginning: group disagrees; middle: members listen; end: they choose a shared plan.
Beginning: a bus arrives; middle: rain falls; end: a goat eats leaves.
Beginning: pupils sleep; middle: a bell rings; end: a spoon breaks.
Beginning: a pencil is red; middle: a desk is wide; end: a window opens.
questions.correctAnswer: Beginning: group disagrees; middle: members listen; end: they choose a shared plan.
questions.explanation: The events are connected and show a clear problem and solution.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan a narrative with a clear conflict and resolution.

questions.prompt: Which sentence gives the clearest evidence that a character is patient?
options: He waited calmly while his partner finished speaking.
He pushed everyone aside at the door.
questions.correctAnswer: He waited calmly while his partner finished speaking.
questions.explanation: Waiting calmly shows patience in action.
questions.learningOutcome: Use textual evidence to support an inference about character.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best fixes the misplaced modifier in Carrying a basket, the market was busy?
options: Carrying a basket, Nimo walked through the busy market.
Carrying a basket, the busy market walked through Nimo.
The market, carrying a basket, was busy.
Busy carrying, a basket was the market.
questions.correctAnswer: Carrying a basket, Nimo walked through the busy market.
questions.explanation: The revision makes it clear that Nimo, not the market, was carrying the basket.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise sentences to place descriptive phrases near the correct noun.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has the most suitable formal tone for requesting permission?
options: May I please borrow the dictionary for this lesson?
I am taking the dictionary whether you like it or not.
questions.correctAnswer: May I please borrow the dictionary for this lesson?
questions.explanation: The sentence is respectful and clearly asks for permission.
questions.learningOutcome: Use formal register for respectful requests.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best concludes a paragraph about the benefits of teamwork?
options: For these reasons, teamwork helps learners complete tasks better.
My shoe was under the desk.
The window was open during break.
A mango can be sweet when ripe.
questions.correctAnswer: For these reasons, teamwork helps learners complete tasks better.
questions.explanation: The conclusion restates the main idea and signals closure.
questions.learningOutcome: Write conclusions that match a paragraph's main idea.

questions.prompt: Which revision best turns this weak sentence into a strong opening for a story: It was a day?
options: At dawn, our class gathered quietly beside the bus for the trip to Fort Jesus.
It was a day and it was there.
The day was a day that happened.
There was a thing in the day.
questions.correctAnswer: At dawn, our class gathered quietly beside the bus for the trip to Fort Jesus.
questions.explanation: The revision gives time, setting, characters, and a clear event.
questions.learningOutcome: Create engaging openings for narratives using setting and action.

questions.prompt: Read: The writer first explains the problem of plastic litter, then gives three ways pupils can reduce it. What is the text structure?
questions.correctAnswer: problem and solution
questions.explanation: The text presents a problem and then offers ways to solve it.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify problem-solution structure in informational texts.

questions.prompt: Which option best evaluates the sentence Everyone knows our class is the best in Kenya?
options: It is a weak claim because it is too broad and unsupported.
It is strong because it includes the word everyone.
It is a fact because Kenya is named.
It is a question because it has many words.
questions.correctAnswer: It is a weak claim because it is too broad and unsupported.
questions.explanation: A strong claim should be reasonable and supported by evidence.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate opinion statements for clarity and support.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best combines cause, contrast, and result?
options: Although the rain delayed us, we shared umbrellas and arrived before assembly.
The rain delayed us the assembly umbrellas before shared.
We arrived although because umbrellas rain.
The rain and assembly were umbrellas.
questions.correctAnswer: Although the rain delayed us, we shared umbrellas and arrived before assembly.
questions.explanation: The sentence shows a difficulty, an action taken, and the final result clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Create complex sentences that connect several related ideas.

questions.prompt: Which response best shows active listening after a partner explains a plan?
options: So you suggest we collect materials first, then begin the model.
I was not listening, but continue.
Your plan is finished because I say so.
questions.correctAnswer: So you suggest we collect materials first, then begin the model.
questions.explanation: Restating the partner's idea shows that the listener understood the main points.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate active listening by paraphrasing a speaker's main idea.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best explains why the title A Small Act of Honesty fits a story about returning lost money?
options: The main action is a simple choice to do what is right.
The story must be about a small coin only.
The title proves the story happened in a shop.
The title means the character became rich.
questions.correctAnswer: The main action is a simple choice to do what is right.
questions.explanation: Returning lost money shows honesty, which is the central idea of the title.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how a title connects to a story's main idea.

questions.prompt: Which edit best improves this sentence for clarity: The learners gave them to the teacher after collecting books?
options: After collecting the books, the learners gave the books to the teacher.
The learners gave them after collecting to the teacher books.
After collecting, them gave the learners to teacher.
The books collecting gave them learners teacher.
questions.correctAnswer: After collecting the books, the learners gave the books to the teacher.
questions.explanation: The edit removes the unclear pronoun and orders the action clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise sentences to remove ambiguity and improve clarity.

questions.prompt: Which question best helps a reader analyse a character's motive?
options: Why did the character give away the last bottle of water?
What colour was the bottle cap?
How many letters are in the character's name?
questions.correctAnswer: Why did the character give away the last bottle of water?
questions.explanation: A motive question asks why a character acted in a certain way.
questions.learningOutcome: Ask analytical questions about characters' reasons for acting.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best turns the notes rainwater tank - school garden - healthy vegetables into a clear report sentence?
options: The rainwater tank supplied water to the school garden, helping the vegetables grow well.
Rainwater tank school garden vegetables healthy.
The vegetables tanked rainwater to school healthy.
Garden water healthy school rainwater because tank.
questions.correctAnswer: The rainwater tank supplied water to the school garden, helping the vegetables grow well.
questions.explanation: The sentence connects the notes into one clear idea with cause and result.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop notes into clear report sentences.

questions.prompt: Which title best fits a poem about learners reading together, sharing ideas, and discovering new words?
questions.correctAnswer: The Power of Reading Together
questions.explanation: The title matches the poem's focus on shared reading and learning new vocabulary.
questions.learningOutcome: Create suitable titles for poems based on central ideas.
